text:
Rohit (runtime): quick question  thinking about implementing 'lease hedging' for dedicated pools to reduce cold-start tail. idea is to let admission request N soft leases across shards and use first-granted. thoughts?
Elena (orch): interesting. hedging reduces tail but increases allocation noise. need limits per-tenant or we'll waste a ton of resources.
Sam (sre): if we hedge, we must surface wasted-reservation metrics. ops needs to know how often hedging caused unused prewarm. alert on >5% waste over 15m.
Priya (product): customers will care about billing. if a hedge reserves but isn't used, do we bill? need a user-explainable model.
Rohit (runtime): plan: hedging reservations are cheap ephemeral tokens (TTL 30s). bill only on 'activation' when job starts using the slot. refunds for expired hedges.
Elena (orch): control plane-wise: hedging implies admission proxy talks to multiple operators. prefer local hedging (proxy asks multiple nodes managed by same operator). avoids cross-operator coord.
Sam (sre): still a race: two proxies could both get hedges and then both activate into the same physical GPU. require the node to enforce a short soft-lock on activation. node checks token-id at activation time.
Priya (product): ok on billing if only activated slots bill. how do we explain fallback to hosted? SLA tiers again.
Rohit (runtime): lane config includes: hedging_factor, max_parallel_hedges, prewarm_ttl, activation_grace. admission proxy loads lane configs.
Elena (orch): autoscaler integration: scaler should see "hedge_pressure" metric (hedges outstanding vs hedges timed out). if many hedges timeout, scale up sooner.
Sam (sre): propose metrics: hedge_waste_pct, hedge_activation_latency_p95, hedge_timeouts_per_min, node_activation_conflicts.
Priya (product): also add a customer-visible header in responses when hedging happened and whether they hit a hedge activation or fallback. helps debugging billing disputes.
Rohit (runtime): implementation detail: admission POST /lease { tenant, slots, lane, prefer_local } -> resp { lease_tokens: [id...], chosen_node_hint }. activation uses POST /activate { token_id, node_id }. node validates token and atomically marks slot used.
Elena (orch): reconcile scope: operator should own node-level slot accounting and token validation only. keep pool-level scaling to autoscaler reading metrics. operator remains simple.
Sam (sre): we must avoid token replay. tokens signed by billing service with short TTL and nonce. node verifies signature. logs must include trace_id.
Priya (product): what about burst token slices? customers want short bursts even if committed capacity is low. can we mint per-tenant ephemeral slices from a shared burst pool?
Rohit (runtime): yes: a shared burst pool in billing service. admission requests a slice up to X for tenant. billing responds with slice_id and capacity. admission locally enforces slice consumption.
Elena (orch): keep slice metadata off the operator. operator only sees activation tokens when a slot is being taken. simplifies operator.
Sam (sre): edge cases: when the burst pool hits zero during mass spike, proxies must degrade gracefully to rate limit and emit a clear fallback reason. alert on mass fallback.
Priya (product): SLA language: "best-effort burst up to configured slice; fallbacks may occur when shared burst pool exhausted." simple and honest.
Rohit (runtime): one more: autoscaler hysteresis. when hedge_pressure spikes, scale aggressively; but when pressure drops, wait N minutes proportional to hedging_factor to avoid flapping.
Elena (orch): agree. implement cooldown = base_cooldown + hedging_factor * coeff. scaler keeps simple state.
Sam (sre): add safety: if node-level OOM or prewarm-fail > threshold, disable hedging for that shard for 10m. reduces cascading failures.
ScaleBot: deploy plan: lease-hedging/v1 -> staging at 2026-04-02T02:00:00Z. smoke tests: token race, activation-signature, billing-refund.
Priya (product): next steps: I'll draft customer docs and billing FAQ. also want a short explainer for support.
Rohit (runtime): I'll open RFC with proto sketches and testmatrix.
Elena (orch): I'll mock autoscaler metric feed and sketch operator changes.
Sam (sre): I'll add alerts and dashboards to the runbook.
Rohit (runtime): thanks all. hedging + burst slices may give us much better tail without bloating operator. quick follow-up meeting tomorrow.
